title: TOEFL iBT Reading Practice Test 13
instructions: Read each passage carefully and answer all questions. You have 35 minutes. Questions test factual understanding, vocabulary, inference, and the ability to identify main ideas.

passages.title: The Printing Press and Knowledge Revolution
passages.text:
The Printing Press and Knowledge Revolution is an important subject of modern scientific and scholarly investigation. Researchers have identified several key mechanisms that govern how this phenomenon operates and how it has changed over time.

Early studies of the printing press and knowledge revolution focused on descriptive accounts, but more recent work employs quantitative methods that allow more precise measurement of patterns and processes. This shift has led to more reliable conclusions that can be applied to real-world problems.

The environmental and social implications of the printing press and knowledge revolution are considerable. Changes in conditions can affect biodiversity, human health, economic systems, and cultural practices in ways that researchers are still working to quantify and understand fully.

Technological advances have accelerated progress in understanding the printing press and knowledge revolution. Remote sensing, genetic analysis, computational modelling, and international research collaborations have all contributed to a more nuanced picture of the subject.

Policymakers and practitioners increasingly draw on research about the printing press and knowledge revolution to inform decisions about conservation, public health, urban planning, and resource management. The challenge lies in translating scientific findings into effective action at both local and global scales.

questions.prompt:
Insert the sentence — "The repeated activation of neural pathways during learning or practice triggers the release of neurotransmitters that reinforce synaptic connections." — into the paragraph. The four squares [1] [2] [3] [4] show where it could be added; choose the best position.

The human brain maintains the ability to reorganize itself throughout life, a property fundamental to learning and recovery.

[1] Neuroplasticity describes the brain's capacity to form new neural connections in response to experience and learning. [2] When neurons are repeatedly activated together, synaptic connections between them strengthen through a process called long-term potentiation. [3] This mechanism allows the brain to encode memories and develop new skills by physically altering its structure. [4] Without this remarkable property, individuals would be unable to recover cognitive function following brain injury.
questions.explanation: This sentence explains the consequence of 'neurons repeatedly activated together' (position 2). The phrase 'repeated activation' directly references the condition mentioned, making this the optimal position for this mechanistic detail.

questions.prompt:
Insert the sentence — "The specificity of enzyme-substrate binding depends on complementary shapes and chemical properties, a relationship described by the lock-and-key model." — into the paragraph. The four squares [1] [2] [3] [4] show where it could be added; choose the best position.

Enzymes are biological catalysts that accelerate chemical reactions essential for life processes.

[1] Enzymes function by lowering the activation energy required for chemical reactions, allowing them to proceed millions of times faster than uncatalyzed reactions. [2] The enzyme-substrate complex forms when a substrate molecule enters the enzyme's active site, which is shaped specifically to accommodate that substrate. [3] This interaction positions the substrate in a way that destabilizes its chemical bonds and promotes rapid conversion to product. [4] After the product is released, the enzyme remains unchanged and can bind another substrate molecule.
questions.explanation: This sentence explains the 'specific shaping' of the active site mentioned in position 2. The phrase 'enzyme-substrate binding' directly follows the introduction of the enzyme-substrate complex, making this the logical position for elaboration on molecular recognition.
